heading.en: Building a swimmer, piece by piece

hook.en: Fear can be beaten, but not in one day. Douglas did it with an instructor, a rope and months of patient practice.

objectives.en: Explain how the fear affected Douglas's life
Describe the instructor's method step by step
Explain how Douglas tested himself afterwards

narration.en: Fear can be beaten, but not in one day. Douglas did it with an instructor, a rope and months of patient practice.

body.en: For years the memory of the pool haunted Douglas. Whenever he went near water, the old terror returned. It spoiled fishing trips, canoeing and swimming in the lakes and rivers he loved. He finally decided that he had to get an instructor and learn to swim properly.

points.en: The terror returned near any water
It spoiled fishing, canoeing and swimming
He decided to fight it with an instructor
Will power was his main weapon

narration.en: For years the memory of the pool haunted Douglas. Whenever he went near water, the old terror returned. It spoiled fishing trips, canoeing and swimming in the lakes and rivers he loved.

title.en: How the instructor built a swimmer

narration.en: Let us list what the instructor taught and why.

say.en: First a belt on a rope over a pulley kept him safe, so he could trust the water.
Next he learnt to breathe out with his face under water.
Then to raise his nose and breathe in, building a rhythm.
Then to kick with his legs, relaxed and steady.
Finally he swam alone in lakes to test whether the fear was gone.

body.en: The instructor put a belt around Douglas, attached to a rope that ran over a pulley, and held the end of it as he swam back and forth across the pool. Then he taught him one skill at a time: to put his face under water and breathe out, to raise his nose and breathe in, and then to kick with his legs. Piece by piece he built a swimmer. Even then, Douglas tested himself alone, first in the pool and later in lakes, until the fear was really gone.

points.en: Breathing: exhale under water, inhale above
Kicking with relaxed legs; then the whole stroke
Tested himself alone in lakes until the fear left

narration.en: The instructor put a belt around Douglas, attached to a rope that ran over a pulley, and held the end of it as he swam back and forth across the pool. Then he taught him one skill at a time: to put his face under water and breathe out, to raise his nose and breathe in, and then to kick with his legs. Piece by piece he built a swimmer.

body.en: The training moved from safety to skills to tests: rope first, then breathing, then kicking, then lonely swims in lakes.

narration.en: The training moved from safety to skills to tests: rope first, then breathing, then kicking, then lonely swims in lakes.

problem.en: How did the instructor build a swimmer out of Douglas?

steps.en: Mention the rope, belt and pulley used for safety.
Mention the breathing practice: out under water, in above it.
Mention the leg kicks, practised until the whole stroke came together.

answer.en: The instructor tied a belt round Douglas, attached to a rope over a pulley, and taught him piece by piece: to breathe out under water, breathe in above it and kick his legs, until he could swim.
